name: Pedra Grande
description: A granite dome above Atibaia with an open summit. The climb is steady rather than steep, and the last stretch crosses bare rock, so it is best avoided in the rain.

name: Serra do Japi Reserve
description: A protected forest reserve covering one of the largest surviving blocks of Atlantic forest near the city. Entry is controlled and dogs are not permitted, because the area shelters native wildlife.

name: Mata Santa Genebra
description: A flat forest loop inside the city limits, used as much for birdwatching as for walking. A good first trail, and the shade makes it comfortable even at midday.

name: Bosque dos Jequitibas
description: Paved paths under old jequitiba trees in the centre of Campinas. Short, level and busy at the weekend, which makes it the easiest option on this list for families.

name: Lagoa do Taquaral Loop
description: A flat circuit around the lake at Parque Portugal, shared with runners and cyclists. Lit in the early evening, so it works when a longer trail will not fit in the day.

name: Parque Ecologico Salim
description: Wide gravel paths through an ecological park beside the Atibaia river. Mostly level, with open grass between the wooded sections.

name: Pico do Lopo
description: A long climb to a ridge on the border between Sao Paulo and Minas Gerais. The upper section is exposed grassland, with weather that changes faster than the forest below.

name: Cachoeira dos Pretos
description: A walk to one of the tallest waterfalls in the state. The water is strongest in the rainy months, which is also when the descent is most slippery.

name: Serra do Itapetinga
description: A sustained climb through a state park to a rocky summit. Access is regulated and the gate closes early, so an afternoon start is not an option.

name: Morro do Cristo
description: A short climb above Valinhos with a view across the fig orchards that gave the city its name. Popular at sunset, so parking fills early.

name: Represa Salto Grande
description: A long shoreline walk beside the reservoir, flat and open. Little shade, so an early start matters more here than the distance suggests.

name: Pedra do Bau
description: The hardest walk on this list and the furthest from Campinas. The final section uses fixed ladders and cables on bare rock, and is not suitable for anyone uneasy with height.

name: Parque das Aguas
description: Gentle paths through a spa town park built around mineral springs. Short enough to combine with the climb at Alto da Serra on the same day.

name: Alto da Serra Lookout
description: A climb out of the valley to a lookout over the coffee hills. Steady gradient on a dirt road, with no technical sections.

name: Trilha do Cafe
description: A rural route between old coffee estates, following farm tracks and a disused rail bed. Open country for most of the way, with very little shade.

name: Morro Azul
description: A wooded hill rising from flat farmland, with a short rocky section near the top. Quiet on weekdays and rarely crowded even at the weekend.

name: Mata do Quilombo
description: A small forest fragment preserved inside the urban area, with a marked interpretive loop. Dogs are not allowed because the reserve protects nesting birds.

name: Pedreira do Chapadao
description: A short walk around a former quarry turned into a park, with rock walls on one side and a lake on the other. The shortest route on this list.
